# @arki/failure

> Typed expected failures for TypeScript with no wrapper. A function returns `Value | Failure<...>`, the compiler infers the union, and every caller must check. It is not an effect system and not for bugs.

## Import paths
<!-- llms:start -->
- `@arki/failure`: @arki/failure: typed expected failures returned as plain values, with no wrapper. `FAILURE_ERROR_CODES`, `FailureError`, `UnexpectedFailure`, `assertNever`, `attempt`, `collect`, `defineFailure`, `findCause`, `isFailure`, `match`, `orThrow`, `partition`; and 17 more.
- `@arki/failure/eslint`: the `must-use` and `no-blind-accept` rules. `default`, `mustUse`, `noBlindAccept`.
- `@arki/failure/orpc`: failures at an oRPC boundary. `errorMap`, `orThrowRpc`, `reviveRpcError`; types `DeclaredErrors`, `ErrorMapOf`.
<!-- llms:end -->

## Rules that bite
- A discarded call drops its failure. Turn on `failure/must-use`.
- Check with `isFailure` or `Def.is`. Truthiness does not narrow.
- Misuse throws `FailureError`. Do not catch it; fix the call.
- Failure data schemas must be synchronous and accept their own output.
- A returned failure does not roll back a transaction.
